analysis.title: Sustaining resilience: Year Ahead 2027 – At a Glance, UBS House View
key_insights: UBS CIO base case for 2027 is constructive: solid earnings, continued AI investment and easing inflation. Strong market gains have raised expectations, so the risk-reward for global equities is more balanced.
Government debt is becoming a larger constraint and geopolitics is likely to generate volatility, while economic fundamentals remain the primary driver of returns.
Recommendation is to stay invested but reduce excess concentration, rebalance into fixed income, and broaden returns through commodities, currencies and alternatives.
Equities: favor industrials and health care, prefer the Eurozone, and within tech favor financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization and internally funded investment.
AI: retain exposure but reduce concentration. Favor financially strong hyperscalers and select leaders in compute, foundry and semiconductor equipment.
Power and resources: prioritize established businesses with visible orders and proven execution. Longevity: balance established health care franchises with select innovators.

Volatility: shifting expectations on AI, inflation, government debt and geopolitics should create higher-volatility periods. Capital preservation strategies, structured yield and predefined entry strategies are suggested.
Fixed income is rated Attractive. Prefer intermediate duration (maturities of two to 10 years), and emerging market and high yield bonds on a relative basis, with diversified exposure.

Gold is favored as a diversifier against fiscal, geopolitical and inflation risks. Build broad commodity exposure and copper positions on weakness, supported by demand from power networks, data centers and electrification.
Currencies: favor sterling and select emerging market carry strategies, and use the Swiss franc as a funding currency.
Alternatives: favor hedge funds, operationally focused private equity and secondaries, core and core-plus infrastructure, and select senior-secured private debt.
Four scenarios for December 2027: base case (resilience sustained), upside (Goldilocks), downside I (the yield reset) and downside II (the AI bust).

sector_views.rationale: Favored as part of refocusing equity exposure away from concentrated market leadership.
Favored for equity diversification, balancing established franchises with select innovators in longevity.

Retain AI exposure but reduce concentration. Favor financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization and internally funded investment, plus select compute, foundry and semiconductor equipment leaders.
Build broad commodity exposure and copper positions on weakness, supported by demand from power networks, data centers and electrification.

earnings_insights: Base case expects solid corporate earnings in 2027. Report states earnings have advanced in recent years and higher corporate profits should support further equity gains.

Upside scenario has earnings expectations stronger, broader and longer lasting. Downside I has them falling overall with wide sector dispersion. Downside II has them falling sharply, led by AI sectors.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.50% base, 4.00% upside, 5.25% downside I, 2.00% downside II
macro_indicators.interpretation: Scenario-dependent. Inflation persistence leads to hikes in downside I, while a severe slowdown leads to deep cuts in downside II.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.75% base, 4.00% upside, 5.50% downside I, 3.00% downside II
macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields decline modestly in the base case, rise on inflation and fiscal risk in downside I, and fall as quality bonds outperform in downside II.

macro_indicators.reading: 8,200 base, 9,500 upside, 7,000 downside I, 5,500 downside II
macro_indicators.interpretation: Scenario-based levels, not a single point target. The base case implies modest equity upside.

macro_indicators.reading: 1.16 base, 1.10 upside, 1.12 downside I, 1.20 downside II
5,000 base, 3,800 upside, 4,400 downside I, 5,500 downside II
macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold is highest in the AI bust scenario and lowest in Goldilocks, consistent with its role as a diversifier.

macro_indicators.reading: Resilient (around trend) in base case, strong (above trend) in upside, slower in downside I, severe slowdown in downside II
Gradually eases in base case, eases in upside, sticky in downside I, eases in downside II
macro_indicators.interpretation: Sticky inflation is the main trigger for the yield reset downside.

trade_ideas.description: Build broad commodity exposure and add copper positions on weakness
trade_ideas.rationale: Copper is supported by demand from power networks, data centers and electrification.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold as a portfolio diversifier
trade_ideas.rationale: Gold diversifies against fiscal, geopolitical and inflation risks.

trade_ideas.description: Long sterling and select emerging market carry, with the Swiss franc as funding currency
trade_ideas.rationale: Align currency exposure with future spending and liabilities.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance into intermediate-duration (2-10 year) fixed income, with emerging market and high yield bonds on a relative basis
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields offer income and return potential, and quality bonds improve diversification.

risk_factors: Strong market gains have raised expectations, leaving equity risk-reward more balanced.
Government debt is becoming a larger policy constraint.
Geopolitics is likely to generate volatility.
Inflation proves more persistent than expected, possibly from energy shocks, AI-driven shortages or underlying stickiness, leading to further central bank hikes.
AI capacity growth outstrips demand, weakening utilization, pricing and expected cash returns, with lower capex weighing on employment, credit creation and consumer confidence.
Negative wealth effects could amplify a downturn.
vol_and_positioning: Shifting expectations around AI, inflation, government debt and geopolitics are likely to create periods of higher volatility.
Appropriately sized capital preservation strategies can help reduce drawdown risk.
Structured yield strategies and predefined entry strategies can help investors generate income or build exposure gradually.
Reduce concentration risk through diversification and regular rebalancing.
geopolitical: Geopolitics is expected to remain a source of volatility in the base case.
Upside scenario assumes contained geopolitical tensions.
Downside I cites a possible renewed energy or refined products shock and broader supply disruption.

key_data_points.context: Base case scenario level. Upside 9,500, downside I 7,000, downside II 5,500.

key_data_points.metric: Fed policy rate base case December 2027

key_data_points.anchor: We favor intermediate average duration—maturities of two to 10 years

tension_points.bull_case: Base case and upside have AI capex remaining solid or exceeding expectations, with productivity gains spreading across industries.
tension_points.bear_case: In the AI bust scenario, capacity growth outstrips demand, weakening utilization, pricing and expected cash returns, and capex slows sharply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakening cloud utilization and realized pricing, reduced AI capex guidance, negative earnings revisions.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation gradually eases and bond yields decline modestly in the base case, supporting fixed income.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation proves more persistent, central banks raise rates and government bond yields rise, so stocks and bonds struggle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed energy or refined products shock, hawkish Fed commentary and action, rising inflation expectations, rising sovereign bond stress.
